summary: Talladega National Forest lookout: a CCC wooden tower of 1939 per the register, replaced around 1959-1960 by a steel tower moved from Burgess Point; gone by 2013.

access.note: Inside the Duggar Mountain Wilderness in the Talladega National Forest. A 2013 hike listed the former tower site as a point of interest.

visit.trail_note: A 2013 hike along a section of the Pinhoti Trail over Duggar Mountain listed the former tower site as a point of interest. No current road or trail rules were found.

notes_for_editor: Build date conflict: the register says the CCC completed the wooden tower in 1939, but a Piedmont Journal item dated April 1, 1938 (quoted on Forest Lookouts) already describes a 30-foot wooden structure in use. The register's datasheet note also says the 1939 tower was the second at the site. The story reports both and does not pick one. Removal of the steel tower is not dated in any source read; the 2013 hike notice calls the site removed. Burgess Point origin of the steel tower rests on the register alone. A Komoot listing (user-contributed, not used) describes a Burgess Fire Tower at Bluegrass Point, Clay County, dated 1936, which may be related. The Anniston Outdoor Association hike plan was seen only as a search snippet and not read. Spelling: Duggar in the register, the 2013 notice and the 1938 items; Dugger on the Forest Lookouts page title. No photos added: the register credits Al Pelham for a 1939-1959 photo, but no image URL was extracted.
